
A `definition` rule holds one term, one meaning, in one scope. Its canonical page is `/project/<name>/term/<slug>`, also reachable by id. A definition may carry the concept IRI from `ns/concept.ttl` it defines, so the term, its meaning and the code shape that carries it (a requirement on the `internal/model` type, which `needs` the definition) are three linked rows.

A project's definitions are its glossary, and the instance has one shared glossary: the definitions of the project named by the `glossary_project` setting. The Project Glossary page lists them (WL-REQ-1815). A term used inside a project resolves to the project's definition first, then the instance's. A project definition that narrows an instance term `refines` it. A project definition that reuses a label with a different meaning is allowed; the project copy wins inside the project, and the conflict is visible as two definitions of one label with no edge between them. Worklode's own vocabulary stays in `ns/` (section 14).
